facts.text: Dufferin Grove’s streets were once lined with grand country villas, including Dover Court, Rush Holme, and Heydon Villa.
The neighbourhood sits west of downtown Toronto, bounded by Bloor to the north, Ossington to the east, College to the south, and Dufferin to the west.
Most houses in Dufferin Grove were built between 1890 and 1930, showcasing Victorian, Edwardian, and English Cottage styles.
Dufferin Grove is known for its green streets, large gardens, and a popular community park that attracts families every weekend.
The Dufferin bus links riders to the Dufferin subway station on the Bloor‑Danforth line, while the Dovercourt and Ossington buses connect to Ossington station.
Two elementary schools serve the area: Ossington Old Orchard Public School and Dewson Street Junior Public School.
